title: Silverbridge - Sovereignty & Capacity Extension Sync

EU private VPC pilot and data residency requirements

pricing and contract term options (12 vs 24 month)

Liam to share perf benchmark template, sample prompts and suggested metrics by 2027-10-11

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-06
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Rourke (Redwood) / Priya Desai, Mark Vella, Anita Gomez, Tom Keller (Silverbridge)

Summary: Quick sync ahead of renewal to align on capacity, sovereignty pilot and security next steps. Some noise and overlapping talk in places, auto transcription has minor name errors.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — is the time still good for all?
[00:04] Priya: Yep, perfect.
[00:06] Maya: Great. So agenda — capacity uplift ask, EU private pilot, security artifacts and then pricing/term options. Liam will cover perf and architecture detail.
[00:14] Liam: Hi all, thanks. From the SE side I'll try to map what a two week benchmark window would look like, kinda smoke test the dedicated nodes and get tail-latency numbers. We'll also show a canary rollout pattern.
[00:25] Mark: Real quick — our traffic's been creeping up, roughly 18% month over month for the last quarter. We think steady state uplift for Q1 would be about 20% and we want a 2x burst for marketing spikes.
[00:36] Maya: OK 20% steady, 2x burst. Noted. For pricing, we can show a committed reserved capacity vs flexible burst mix — both 12 and 24 month terms.
[00:44] Tom: Procurement question — do you have a sample contract amendment for a top up? Also how does billing for burst actually meter?
[00:52] Maya: We'll attach a pricing spreadsheet and a sample amendment. Burst is metered as overage tokens on hosted — for Dedicated we do configured burst pools that are billed differently, we'll put examples in the sheet.
[01:02] Anita: From security, primary ask is EU data residency — we need a private VPC pilot in eu-west-1 and, second, SOC 2 Type II plus any ISO docs you have, and a runbook for an on-prem option. Also KMS/HSM integration notes.
[01:18] Liam: Understood. For private VPC we have a private control plane option and an on-prem variant. There are some differences: private VPC still uses our control plane but with customer-managed networking and you can ship logs to your SIEM; on-prem is full air-gapped with the onprem bundle. For KMS we integrate via standard KMS APIs but if you have an HSM we can discuss an HSM-backed flow — there are additional ops steps.
[01:39] Priya: Do you have a one pager for the differences? We want something to show execs.
[01:43] Maya: Yes, we'll share a short comparison doc (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC vs On-prem) with ops and security notes.
[01:50] Mark: For perf — can you run with quantized model or do we need to use full fp16 to match our current quality? We saw differences when we tried quantized in-house.
[01:58] Liam: Good question. Quantization can give big cost/latency wins, but it's model dependent — there can be small diff in rare tokens. Our plan: run a split benchmark — baseline full fp16 variant and a quantized profile (8-bit or 4-bit depending on model) and measure ROUGE-ish / semantic drift on your prompts. We'll surface latency p95/p99 and token cost.
[02:19] Priya: How long would that take?
[02:22] Liam: We recommend two weeks to get stable results across your traffic distribution. We can also do a canary for a subset of production over a week to validate fallbacks.
[02:31] Tom: If we do private VPC, what's the provisioning lead time? We have a compliance window in Nov so ideally pilot in the second half of Oct.
[02:40] Maya: For private VPC pilot in EU region we usually see 2-3 weeks to provision the private stub and coordinate network peering, sometimes a bit longer if there's a weird firewall policy. On-prem lead time is typically longer — depends on site ops and airgap validation.
[02:55] Anita: We need logs to be forwarded to our Splunk and a SOC-friendly audit trail. Is that standard?
[02:59] Liam: Yes, we can forward audit logs via secure syslog / S3 export with encryption. RBAC and token-level tracing is available. We'll include a sample log schema.
[03:10] Mark: One more — latency SLOs. We need p95 under 250ms for interactive endpoints. Is that achievable in EU private?
[03:18] Liam: Depends on model and instance type. For smaller models yes, for big gen models it's tight. We'll run the benchmark and include recommended hardware and kernel selection. We also have automatic fallback to a cheaper variant for lower-latency needs.
[03:31] Priya: Competitors we looked at had easy on-prem packaging but poor observability. You folks have the console that shows token costs per route, right?
[03:39] Maya: Yep console gives per-route token-level cost, latency breakdown, and per-model dashboards. That's one of the differentiators we highlight.
[03:46] Tom: For contract term — what's your recommendation? 12 or 24 months? We want flexibility but also cost predictability.
[03:51] Maya: For a SMB-ish growth pattern, 12 months with a modest commitment + burst credits gives flexibility. If you want unit discounts and reserved pricing, 24 months gets better rates. We'll show both on the pricing sheet.
[04:02] Anita: Any regulatory notes for data residency? We need data at-rest encryption, KMS control, and audit logs. Also who has access to platform logs?
[04:11] Liam: Access is RBAC controlled; we can integrate with SAML SSO, and all logs can be exported to your SIEM so you retain control. For KMS, customer-managed key options are available on private deployments.
[04:23] Priya: Okay timeline wise — we need the pilot up by end of Oct to feed the Nov compliance review. Are those dates realistic?
[04:29] Maya: Tight but doable if we start immediately; provisioning + network approvals + perf window will need a compressed schedule.
[04:36] Mark: We'll provide expected traffic patterns today and confirm EU region by Tuesday.
[04:41] Maya: Perfect. We'll also include an example rollback/canary plan in the doc pack.
[04:45] Liam: One practical note — for the benchmark we'll want a retained prompt set and expected response lengths. If you have a saved corpus, share a representative sample (anonymized) and we'll run it through both variants.
[04:58] Priya: We'll get that to you, but might need a quick NDA addendum for data sample sharing?
[05:03] Tom: Procurement will check but we usually have a sample sharing clause.
[05:07] Liam: We can accept anonymized synthetic prompts too for initial runs if that speeds things up.
[05:11] [small cross talk — audio glitch]
[05:22] Maya: Alright let's recap next steps — I'll send pricing + amendment, Liam sends perf template and quantization notes, Anita will enumerate extra compliance artifacts, Mark sends traffic profile. Security deep-dive to be scheduled.
[05:36] Priya: That works. Do we need signature on something to start provisioning?
[05:39] Maya: For private VPC pilot we typically need an SOW and the network sheet signed; we'll include a pilot SOW draft with the pricing doc.
[05:46] Tom: Thanks. Anything else?
[05:48] Maya: No, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in writing.
[05:51] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional proper nouns mis-typed (e.g., "GigaServe" was auto-capitalized), fillers like "uh" and "you know" present.
